verses.original: Ἰάκωβος Θεοῦ καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος Ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ Διασπορᾷ Χαίρειν
verses.transliteration: Iakōbos Theou kai Kyriou Iēsou Christou doulos Tais dōdeka phylais tais en tē Diaspora Chairein
verses.literal: James a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion Greetings
verses.literalPt: TIAGO, servo de Deus, e do Senhor Jesus Cristo, às doze tribos que andam dispersas, saúde.

verses.original: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε ἀδελφοί μου ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις
verses.transliteration: Pasan charan hēgēsasthe adelphoi mou hotan peirasmois peripesēte poikilois
verses.literal: Consider it pure joy my brothers when you encounter trials of many kinds
verses.literalPt: Meus irmãos, tende grande gozo quando cairdes em várias tentações;

verses.original: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν
verses.transliteration: ginōskontes hoti to dokimion hymōn tēs pisteōs katergazetai hypomonēn
verses.literal: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance
verses.literalPt: Sabendo que a prova da vossa fé opera a paciência.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι
verses.transliteration: hē de hypomonē ergon teleion echetō hina ēte teleioi kai holoklēroi en mēdeni leipomenoi
verses.literal: Allow perseverance to finish its work so that you may be mature and complete not lacking anything
verses.literalPt: Tenha, porém, a paciência a sua obra perfeita, para que sejais perfeitos e completos, sem faltar em coisa alguma.

verses.original: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος Θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ei de tis hymōn leipetai sophias aiteitō para tou didontos Theou pasin haplōs kai mē oneidizontos kai dothēsetai autō
verses.literal: Now if any of you lacks wisdom he should ask . . . God who gives generously to all without finding fault and it will be given to him
verses.literalPt: E, se algum de vós tem falta de sabedoria, peça-a a Deus, que a todos dá liberalmente, e o não lança em rosto, e ser-lhe-á dada.

verses.original: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει μηδὲν διακρινόμενος ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ
verses.transliteration: aiteitō de en pistei mēden diakrinomenos ho gar diakrinomenos eoiken klydōni thalassēs anemizomenō kai rhipizomenō
verses.literal: But he must ask in faith without doubting because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea blown and tossed by the wind
verses.literalPt: Peça-a, porém, com fé, em nada duvidando; porque o que duvida é semelhante à onda do mar, que é levada pelo vento, e lançada de uma para outra parte.

verses.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου
verses.transliteration: mē gar oiesthō ho anthrōpos ekeinos hoti lēmpsetai ti para tou Kyriou
verses.literal: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord
verses.literalPt: Não pense tal homem que receberá do Senhor alguma coisa.

verses.original: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: anēr dipsychos akatastatos en pasais tais hodois autou
verses.literal: He is a double-minded man unstable in all his ways
verses.literalPt: O homem de coração dobre é inconstante em todos os seus caminhos.

verses.original: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kauchasthō de ho adelphos ho tapeinos en tō hypsei autou
verses.literal: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position
verses.literalPt: Mas glorie-se o irmão abatido na sua exaltação,

verses.original: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται
verses.transliteration: ho de plousios en tē tapeinōsei autou hoti hōs anthos chortou pareleusetai
verses.literal: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position because he will pass away like a flower of the field
verses.literalPt: E o rico em seu abatimento; porque ele passará como a flor da erva.

verses.original: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται
verses.transliteration: aneteilen gar ho hēlios syn tō kausōni kai exēranen ton chorton kai to anthos autou exepesen kai hē euprepeia tou prosōpou autou apōleto houtōs kai ho plousios en tais poreiais autou maranthēsetai
verses.literal: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant its flower falls and its beauty . . . . . . . . . is lost So too the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits
verses.literalPt: Porque sai o sol com ardor, e a erva seca, e a sua flor cai, e a formosa aparência do seu aspecto perece; assim se murchará também o rico em seus caminhos.

verses.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Makarios anēr hos hypomenei peirasmon hoti dokimos genomenos lēmpsetai ton stephanon tēs zōēs hon epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton
verses.literal: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial because when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him
verses.literalPt: Bem-aventurado o homem que suporta a tentação; porque, quando for provado, receberá a coroa da vida, a qual o Senhor tem prometido aos que o amam.

verses.original: Μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πειράζομαι ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα
verses.transliteration: Mēdeis peirazomenos legetō hoti Apo Theou peirazomai ho gar Theos apeirastos estin kakōn peirazei de autos oudena
verses.literal: When tempted no one should say God is tempting me For God cannot be tempted by evil nor does He tempt anyone
verses.literalPt: Ninguém, sendo tentado, diga: De Deus sou tentado; porque Deus não pode ser tentado pelo mal, e a ninguém tenta.

verses.original: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος
verses.transliteration: hekastos de peirazetai hypo tēs idias epithymias exelkomenos kai deleazomenos
verses.literal: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed
verses.literalPt: Mas cada um é tentado, quando atraído e engodado pela sua própria concupiscência.

verses.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον
verses.transliteration: eita hē epithymia syllabousa tiktei hamartian hē de hamartia apotelestheisa apokyei thanaton
verses.literal: Then after desire has conceived it gives birth to sin and sin when it is full-grown gives birth to death
verses.literalPt: Depois, havendo a concupiscência concebido, dá à luz o pecado; e o pecado, sendo consumado, gera a morte.

verses.original: Μὴ πλανᾶσθε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί
verses.transliteration: Mē planasthe adelphoi mou agapētoi
verses.literal: Do not be deceived my beloved brothers
verses.literalPt: Não erreis, meus amados irmãos.

verses.original: πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς τῶν φώτων παρ’ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα
verses.transliteration: pasa dosis agathē kai pan dōrēma teleion anōthen estin katabainon apo tou Patros tōn phōtōn par’ hō ouk eni parallagē ē tropēs aposkiasma
verses.literal: Every good and perfect gift is from above coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights with whom there is no change or shifting shadow
verses.literalPt: Toda a boa dádiva e todo o dom perfeito vem do alto, descendo do Pai das luzes, em quem não há mudança nem sombra de variação.

verses.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων
verses.transliteration: boulētheis apekyēsen hēmas logō alētheias eis to einai hēmas aparchēn tina tōn autou ktismatōn
verses.literal: He chose to give us birth . . . through the word of truth that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation
verses.literalPt: Segundo a sua vontade, ele nos gerou pela palavra da verdade, para que fôssemos como primícias das suas criaturas.

verses.original: Ἴστε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν
verses.transliteration: Iste adelphoi mou agapētoi estō de pas anthrōpos tachys eis to akousai bradys eis to lalēsai bradys eis orgēn
verses.literal: My beloved brothers understand this Everyone . . . should be quick to listen slow to speak and slow to anger
verses.literalPt: Portanto, meus amados irmãos, todo o homem seja pronto para ouvir, tardio para falar, tardio para se irar.

verses.original: ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται
verses.transliteration: orgē gar andros dikaiosynēn Theou ouk ergazetai
verses.literal: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires
verses.literalPt: Porque a ira do homem não opera a justiça de Deus.

verses.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: dio apothemenoi pasan rhyparian kai perisseian kakias en prautēti dexasthe ton emphyton logon ton dynamenon sōsai tas psychas hymōn
verses.literal: Therefore get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil and humbly accept the word planted in you which can save your souls
verses.literalPt: Por isso, rejeitando toda a imundícia e superfluidade de malícia, recebei com mansidão a palavra em vós enxertada, a qual pode salvar as vossas almas.

verses.original: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς
verses.transliteration: Ginesthe de poiētai logou kai mē akroatai monon paralogizomenoi heautous
verses.literal: Be doers of the word and not hearers only Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves
verses.literalPt: E sede cumpridores da palavra, e não somente ouvintes, enganando-vos com falsos discursos.

verses.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ
verses.transliteration: hoti ei tis akroatēs logou estin kai ou poiētēs houtos eoiken andri katanoounti to prosōpon tēs geneseōs autou en esoptrō
verses.literal: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks - at his face in a mirror
verses.literalPt: Porque, se alguém é ouvinte da palavra, e não cumpridor, é semelhante ao homem que contempla ao espelho o seu rosto natural;

verses.original: κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν
verses.transliteration: katenoēsen gar heauton kai apelēlythen kai eutheōs epelatheto hopoios ēn
verses.literal: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like
verses.literalPt: Porque se contempla a si mesmo, e vai-se, e logo se esquece de como era.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται
verses.transliteration: ho de parakypsas eis nomon teleion ton tēs eleutherias kai parameinas ouk akroatēs epilēsmonēs genomenos alla poiētēs ergou houtos makarios en tē poiēsei autou estai
verses.literal: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law - of freedom and continues to do so not being a forgetful hearer but an effective doer he will be blessed in what he does
verses.literalPt: Aquele, porém, que atenta bem para a lei perfeita da liberdade, e nisso persevera, não sendo ouvinte esquecidiço, mas fazedor da obra, este tal será bem-aventurado no seu feito.

verses.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία
verses.transliteration: Ei tis dokei thrēskos einai mē chalinagōgōn glōssan autou alla apatōn kardian autou toutou mataios hē thrēskeia
verses.literal: If anyone considers himself . . . religious and yet does not bridle his tongue he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless
verses.literalPt: Se alguém entre vós cuida ser religioso, e não refreia a sua língua, antes engana o seu coração, a religião desse é vã.

verses.original: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου
verses.transliteration: thrēskeia kathara kai amiantos para tō Theō kai Patri hautē estin episkeptesthai orphanous kai chēras en tē thlipsei autōn aspilon heauton tērein apo tou kosmou
verses.literal: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this to care for orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world
verses.literalPt: A religião pura e imaculada para com Deus, o Pai, é esta: Visitar os órfãos e as viúvas nas suas tribulações, e guardar-se da corrupção do mundo.
